title: K-th Nearest Obstacle Queries
summary: On an infinite 2D plane, you are given a positive integer k and a series of queries to build obstacles.
statement: On an infinite 2D plane, you are given a positive integer k and a series of queries to build obstacles. Each query specifies coordinates (x, y) to place an obstacle. After each query, determine the distance of the k^th nearest obstacle to the origin. If fewer than k obstacles exist, return -1. The distance from the origin to an obstacle at (x, y) is |x| + |y|. Initially, no obstacles are present.
constraints: queries are distinct integer coordinates and k is positive.
After inserting each obstacle, rank all Manhattan distances |x|+|y|.
Return the kth-smallest distance, or -1 while fewer than k obstacles exist.
hints: Only the k smallest distances can affect the kth-smallest value.
Maintain those distances in a size-k max-heap represented by negatives.
Push each distance; when size exceeds k, remove the largest retained distance.
Discarded distances are at least as large as every retained candidate, so the heap maximum is exactly rank k.
editorial: Discarded distances are at least as large as every retained candidate, so the heap maximum is exactly rank k.
